rules.zh: 固定用語本身不作變化在這個固定用語中，通常不會把 it 改為 this 或 that，也不會隨主句時態改變 is。
rules.en: The fixed expression does not change Use: for what it is worth Do not normally change it to: for what this is worth for what that is worth for what it was worth

rules.zh: 詞語【I think】並不是固定部分這個句型並不只用來提出個人意見。僅供參考，我認為第一個設計較清楚。 姑且一提，辦公室在五時關門。 不管這個建議是否有用，請保留收據副本。 那名顧客看來很困惑；這只是我的觀察。 我可以在會議後留下來；不知道這項幫助是否有用。
rules.en: “I think” is optional The structure is not limited to personal opinions. Opinion: For what it is worth, I think the first design is clearer. Information: For what it is worth, the office closes at five. Advice: For what it is worth, keep a copy of the receipt. Observation: The customer seemed confused, for what it is worth. Offer: I can stay after the meeting, for what it is worth.

rules.zh: 它評論的是訊息是否有用它不一定表示資料不真確。它表示說話者不肯定對方會否覺得這項訊息有用、相關、重要或有價值。說話者不一定認為這項事實是假的，而是不肯定它是否重要或有用。
rules.en: It comments on the value of the message For what it is worth does not necessarily mean that the information is untrue. It means that the speaker is uncertain whether the message will be useful, relevant, important or valued by the listener. For what it is worth, the witness changed his statement twice. The speaker is not necessarily saying that this fact is false. The speaker is saying that its importance or usefulness is uncertain.

rules.zh: 不宜過度使用只有當說話者確實不肯定內容是否有用，或希望降低語氣強度時，這個用語才最自然。說話者通常沒有理由懷疑這項基本事實是否有用，因此用法可能顯得不自然。
rules.en: Do not overuse it The expression works best when there is a real reason to be modest or uncertain about the usefulness of the message. Unnecessary: For what it is worth, water freezes at 0°C. The speaker normally has no reason to question the usefulness or value of this basic fact.

rules.zh: 口語中常使用縮寫，但本練習使用完整形式。兩者意思相同；為了讓學生穩定掌握完整結構，本練習的所有答案均使用【for what it is worth】。
rules.en: The contracted form is common, but this exercise uses the full form Common contracted form: For what it’s worth, I agree with you. Target form in this exercise: For what it is worth, I agree with you.

rules.zh: 有時可以使用其他自然位置三句都可以自然成立，主要分別在於說話者把補充語放在哪個位置。參考答案為每題提供一個建議版本。如果學生使用另一個自然位置，而句型、標點和意思均正確也可以接受。它表示說話者承認自己的意見或資料未必有用、重要或受到重視。僅供參考，我認為這個計劃很合理。
rules.en: Other natural positions may sometimes be possible For what it is worth, the second plan seems safer. The second plan, for what it is worth, seems safer. The second plan seems safer, for what it is worth. All three sentences can be natural. Their main difference is where the speaker places the parenthetical comment. The answer key gives one preferred model answer for each question. Another position may also receive credit if: the complete expression is used the punctuation is correct the original meaning is preserved the final sentence sounds natural. Differences from Similar Structures For what it is worth It admits that the opinion or information may not be useful, important or valued. For what it is worth, I think the plan is sensible.

rules.zh: 只是表明這是個人意見，不一定含有「這個意見可能並不重要」的謙遜意思。在我看來，這個計劃很合理。 僅供參考，我認為這個計劃很合理。 第二句的語氣較保留和謙遜。用來提出說話者認為對方應該知道的資料。通知你一聲，辦公室在五時關門。 姑且一提，辦公室在五時關門。 第一句較直接；第二句則表示這項資料未必有用。
rules.en: In my opinion In my opinion simply identifies a personal view. It does not necessarily suggest that the view may be unimportant. In my opinion In my opinion, the plan is sensible. The second sentence sounds more cautious and modest. For your information For your information introduces information that the speaker thinks the listener should know. For your information For your information, the office closes at five. For what it is worth, the office closes at five. The first can sound direct. The second suggests that the information may or may not be useful.

rules.zh: 這是另一個不同的固定用語。意思是：請自行判斷這項資料有多可信或有多大價值。我聽說公司可能搬遷，但這項消息是否可信，請你自行判斷。 姑且一提，我聽說公司可能搬遷。 第一句要求聽者自行評估資料；第二句則謙遜地提出資料。這個結構表示某事具有足夠價值，值得採取某個行動。這份報告值得閱讀。 這間博物館值得參觀。 這個意思與固定用語 for what it is worth 不同。
rules.en: Take it for what it is worth This is a different expression. Take it for what it is worth means: Judge the information yourself and decide how much you trust or value it. I heard that the company may move, but take that information for what it is worth. Compare: For what it is worth, I heard that the company may move. The first tells the listener to evaluate the information. The second modestly introduces the information. It is worth + noun / V-ing This structure says that something is valuable, useful or important enough to deserve an action. It is worth reading the report. The museum is worth a visit. This meaning is different from the fixed expression for what it is worth.

benefits.zh: 令意見不會顯得過於強硬你不會把自己的意見說成唯一正確答案，而是讓對方自行判斷是否有用。第二句較像提出個人建議，而不是命令對方。
benefits.en: It makes opinions sound less forceful Instead of presenting your opinion as the only correct answer, you show that the listener is free to decide how useful it is. Direct: You should reject the offer. Softer: For what it is worth, I would reject the offer.

benefits.zh: 顯示謙遜態度這個用語表示你不會假設自己的意見特別重要，能減少自以為是的感覺。
benefits.en: It shows modesty The expression shows that you do not assume that your opinion is especially important.

benefits.zh: 幫助你提出未必相關的資料有時你擁有一項可能有幫助的資料或觀察，但不肯定它是否與當前問題相關。姑且一提，去年也發生過同一問題。 這個用語讓你提出資料，而不會聲稱它一定能解決問題。
benefits.en: It helps you offer uncertain information Sometimes you have a fact or observation that may help, but you are unsure whether it is relevant. For what it is worth, the same problem occurred last year. The expression allows you to contribute without claiming that the information will definitely solve the problem.

benefits.zh: 令不同意見更委婉使用這個句型，可以在提出不同意見時降低衝突感。
benefits.en: It can make disagreement more tactful For what it is worth, I preferred the original proposal. This sounds less confrontational than: The original proposal was better.

benefits.zh: 提供靈活的句子位置你可以把這個用語放在句首、句中或句末，增加句式變化。這樣可以避免所有句子都使用完全相同的排列方式。
benefits.en: It gives you flexible sentence positions You can place the expression at the beginning, in the middle or at the end of a sentence. This prevents every sentence from following exactly the same pattern.
